Izyaslav New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This record contains a chronological inconsistency worth flagging: it states that in the early 18th century, a descendant of the Baal Shem Tov, Rabbi Mordechai, served as the town's cantor — but the Baal Shem Tov himself was only born around 1698 and lived until 1760, making a descendant serving that early essentially impossible; this is likely a source error in either the name, relationship, or date. Izyaslav's Jewish community, established in the 16th century, survived the Khmelnytsky uprising, a 1708 Cossack pogrom, and two separate blood libel accusations in 1747 and 1830. Rabbi Jacob Shimon Shapiro (1772–1811) founded a Hasidic dynasty in the town. In 1942, 5,000 ghetto prisoners were executed, following the murder of 1,000 Jews the previous August. In the 1990s, the Einikite Jewish culture society was established. This is the newer of Izyaslav's two Jewish cemeteries, still operating today.
